title: Add RecipeHeroHeader view
description: Create RecipeHeroHeader.swift. The view renders a hero area at fixed ~240 pt height (~5:3 aspect ratio). It calls RecipeImageLoader asynchronously; if an image loads, it fills the area (ContentMode.fill, clipped); if not, it renders a .tint-colored block with fork.knife SF Symbol centered. A gradient overlay darkens the lower portion for legibility. The recipe title (Recipe.metadata["title"] or filename-minus-extension fallback) is overlaid at the bottom in white .title typography. An xmark.circle.fill dismiss button sits top-leading on a .regularMaterial circular background. Fixed height is preserved regardless of image presence.
acceptance_criteria: Hero area is always ~240 pt tall regardless of image presence.
Image fills the area with ContentMode.fill and is clipped to bounds.
Fallback renders fork.knife centered on a .tint-colored block of the same height.
Gradient overlay applied over the lower portion of the image/placeholder.
Title rendered in white .title font at the bottom of the hero.
xmark.circle.fill button at top-leading position with .regularMaterial circular background.
Dismiss button has an explicit accessibility label.
View delegates all file I/O to RecipeImageLoader.

handoff_summary.completed: Created CookbookApp/Recipes/RecipeHeroHeader.swift. All eight acceptance criteria satisfied. Build passes against the main project xcodeproj.
handoff_summary.remaining: Visual verification of the rendered hero (gradient, image fill, dismiss button) requires a human on device or simulator — agents cannot render UI. The title currently uses RecipeFile.displayName (filename-minus-extension) since RecipeFile does not expose CookbookCore Metadata; a future bead could wire up metadata["title"] if a parsed Recipe is passed to the detail sheet.
handoff_summary.risks: The gradient uses Color.black.opacity(0.65) which is technically a non-semantic color, but is required as a legibility overlay technique — not a themeable surface color. The view is not yet wired up in RecipesListView's sheet; that integration is a separate concern.
handoff_summary.next_action: Tester agent should write snapshot or structure tests for RecipeHeroHeader: verify 240pt height is preserved in both image and fallback states, title text is present, and accessibility label on the dismiss button is set.
handoff_summary.conflict_risks: No conflicts expected. RecipeHeroHeader.swift is a new file with no overlap with sibling beads. RecipesListView.swift is not modified; integration of this header into the sheet is deferred.
handoff_summary.design_decisions: 1. Title source: RecipeFile.displayName used instead of CookbookCore Recipe.metadata["title"] because RecipeFile does not carry parsed metadata; displayName already handles filename-minus-extension fallback as specified. 2. Dismiss button: xmark.circle.fill symbol with .secondary foreground and .regularMaterial Circle background — matches spec literally without double-rendered circle artifacts. 3. Gradient uses Color.black.opacity(0.65) as a standard image-overlay legibility technique, not a semantic surface color. 4. Image task is keyed on recipe.url so it reloads if the recipe changes.
handoff_summary.test_coverage_notes: No tests written (tester agent responsibility). Suggested coverage: fixed frame height in both states, fallback symbol presence, dismiss button accessibility label, RecipeImageLoader delegation (no direct file reads in view).
handoff_summary.known_limitations: Visual rendering (gradient appearance, image fill quality, button position) not verified — agents cannot render UI. RecipeFile.displayName may include the full filename if extension is not .cook; this is pre-existing behaviour in displayName, not a bug introduced here.

conflict_risks: No conflicts expected. RecipeHeroHeader.swift is a new file with no overlap with sibling beads. RecipesListView.swift is not modified; integration of this header into the sheet is deferred.
